title: Unique descent of the canonical affine reverse comparison
statement: Let A,B be commutative rings, φ:B→A, f=Spec(φ), i∈ℤ, with derived scheme-module categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. There is a unique natural isomorphism τ:H^i Rf_*→f_* H^i on D_QCoh(Spec A) whose component at Q(I), for every K-injective complex I with quasi-coherent cohomology, is H^i of the canonical isomorphism Rf_*Q(I)→Q(f_*I), followed by the localization/homology factor, the explicit left exact reverse homology comparison [def-pc-left-exact-homology-comparison], and f_* of the inverse localization/homology factor at I. This determines τ including its inverse by literal equality.

source.place: 0AVW, proof, affine cohomology display; 08D4, bound-one truncation comparison on inverse images of affine opens.

proof.text: Kernel/cokernel universal properties make the explicit comparison natural for chain maps. Homotopic maps agree on homology, so this descends to the K-injective homotopy category.

On each affine open V of Spec B, its inverse image W is affine. Apply the degree-i lower-truncation comparison for derived sections on W and the upper-truncation comparison for the left exact section functor. These remove the two tails in degree i. Track the canonical truncation maps through the kernel-lift and homology-projection formulas proved in def-pc-left-exact-homology-comparison; their universal properties identify the resulting comparison with the displayed reverse map. Affine acyclicity makes this comparison invertible. Invertibility on the affine basis implies invertibility of the sheaf morphism.

The K-injective homotopy category is equivalent to the derived category. Transport the reverse comparison through this equivalence and the right-derived-unit computation. All objects admit K-injective representatives; naturality with those representative isomorphisms determines every component and proves uniqueness.
